summary: Citicoline (CDP-choline) is an endogenous nucleotide used as a neuroprotective and nootropic agent, mainly in ischemic stroke recovery, post-stroke cognitive impairment, vascular/age-related cognitive decline, and as an adjunct in glaucoma. It serves as an intermediate in the synthesis of phosphatidylcholine, a key neuronal membrane phospholipid, and supports acetylcholine production. It is marketed as a prescription drug in several countries (e.g. Europe, Japan, India) and sold as a dietary supplement in the US; it is not FDA-approved as a drug.

moa: Citicoline is hydrolyzed in the gut and tissues to cytidine and choline, which are reincorporated to regenerate cytidine-5'-diphosphocholine intracellularly. As a rate-limiting intermediate in the Kennedy pathway, it promotes synthesis of phosphatidylcholine and other structural phospholipids of neuronal membranes, aiding membrane repair and integrity. It also provides choline for acetylcholine synthesis, increases dopamine and norepinephrine availability, reduces free-fatty-acid release and phospholipase activation during ischemia, and limits glutamate-mediated excitotoxicity and oxidative damage—conferring neuroprotective and neurorestorative effects.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to citicoline or any excipient

preg: Adequate, well-controlled human data in pregnancy are insufficient. Although citicoline is an endogenous compound, it should be avoided during pregnancy unless the expected benefit clearly outweighs potential risk, under specialist advice.
lact: Data on excretion in human milk and effects on the breastfed infant are insufficient. Use with caution during breastfeeding; weigh benefit against potential risk or withhold treatment.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is established; pharmacokinetic data in renal impairment are limited. Use with caution and clinical monitoring.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is established; data in hepatic impairment are limited. Use with caution and clinical monitoring.

pearls: Not FDA-approved; record pending clinical review. Marketed as a prescription drug in Europe/Japan/India and sold as a dietary supplement in the US.
High oral bioavailability (~95%); rapidly hydrolyzed to cytidine and choline and resynthesized to CDP-choline intracellularly
Generally well tolerated with a favorable safety profile; serious adverse events are uncommon
Stroke evidence is mixed—some trials (e.g. ICTUS) did not show clear benefit in acute ischemic stroke; benefit may be greater in cognitive recovery and milder strokes
Choline component supports acetylcholine synthesis, the basis for use in cognitive disorders
missed: Take the missed oral dose as soon as remembered, unless it is almost time for the next dose; do not double up. Resume the regular schedule. Parenteral doses are given under medical supervision.
overdose: Citicoline has a wide safety margin and overdose is rarely associated with serious toxicity. Excess may cause gastrointestinal upset, headache, or, with cholinergic excess, hypotension/bradycardia. Management is supportive and symptomatic; there is no specific antidote.
